title: guard-shared-stash.sh has the same backslash fail-open in split_segments() that objectstack#11131 closed in the bash checkout guard
body:
Measured while porting the `guard-main-checkout-bash.sh` fix family (#5789, objectstack PR objectstack-ai/objectstack#11278). **Out of scope there** — that card is a verbatim port and explicitly forbids touching other hooks — so recorded here instead of folded in.

> 🔧 **Body repaired by the PM seat (`session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`).** The original filing was **truncated mid-sentence** by GitHub's body sanitizer, which eats less-than fragments; it ended at "The `<". The measurement survived but the explanation after it did not. This body restores the full finding, with every angle bracket written in words. Nothing in the original measurement is changed — only completed.

## The observation

`.claude/hooks/guard-shared-stash.sh`'s `split_segments()` has **no backslash branch**.

Outside quotes, a backslash escapes the next character — so an escaped backslash-doublequote opens no quoted region at all. Without that branch, the pass reads the doublequote as opening a region that never closes, goes inert for every separator behind it, and collapses the whole command into a single segment whose head word is the harmless one. The real command behind the separator is then seen as a mere argument of `echo`.

That is the same shape objectstack#11131 closed in `guard-main-checkout-bash.sh`, with the same consequence class: a real `git stash` behind such an escape is waved through.

## Measured

Fed as the PreToolUse payload shape (`{cwd, tool_name:"Bash", tool_input:{command}}`) against this repo's `guard-shared-stash.sh` at `ad0f5f11f`:

| command | verdict |
| --- | --- |
| `git stash` | **blocked** — control: the guard works |
| `echo` backslash-doublequote, then `;`, then `git stash` | **ALLOWED** — the hole |

The control matters: without it, "ALLOWED" could mean the harness never reached the guard rather than that the guard let it past.

## Scope of the hole — what does and does not reproduce

- **The backslash half (objectstack#11131) reproduces**, and it reproduces in **both repos' copies** of `guard-shared-stash.sh`.
- **The comment-heredoc half (objectstack#11133) does NOT reproduce here** — `guard-shared-stash.sh` has no `strip_heredocs()` pass to carry that defect. Only the first of the two upstream fixes has an analogue on this hook.

## Why this matters more than its size suggests

`guard-shared-stash.sh` is the enforcement behind the **⛔ Never `git stash`** rule in both repos' `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`. That rule exists because the stash stack lives in the common `.git` directory and is therefore shared across every worktree: two agents stashing in their own worktrees push and pop the *same* LIFO stack, `pop` reports success, and the only symptom is another agent's files appearing in your `git status` — after which a `git add -A` merges their work into your PR. It has already cost two parallel agents their in-flight changes (objectui#3430).

A fail-open in this guard therefore does not merely admit a discouraged command; it admits the one command whose failure mode silently corrupts a *different* agent's work. The rule still outranks the hook, so this is not a live breach — but the hook is the backstop for the case where an agent does not know the rule.

## Suggested fix

Port the `split_segments()` backslash branch from `guard-main-checkout-bash.sh` (as landed by objectstack#11131 and, in this repo, by PR #6046) into `guard-shared-stash.sh`, and add the corresponding cases to `.claude/hooks/guard-shared-stash.selftest.sh` — the file's own instruction is to re-run that selftest on any change to the hook.

⚠️ Whoever takes this: `.claude/**` is a **governed surface** in both repos — draft PR, human merge.

## Cross-repo

The same hole is present in objectstack's copy. Sibling card filed there; the two should be fixed with the same patch shape to preserve the declared copy parity.

Refs: objectstack#11131 · objectstack PR #11278 · objectui#5789 / PR #6046 · objectui#3430.
